explain: To one person: _Salvē_ and _intrā_. Both are commands to a single person. A guest (_hospes_) was sacred to a Roman, and the host welcomed him warmly.
distractors: _salvēte_ is to several people. One guest: _salvē_.
_intrāte_ is to several people. One guest: _intrā_.
When you speak to someone, use the vocative: _hospes_, not the accusative _hospitem_.

explain: _sedē_ is the command to one person (from _sedeō_), and _quaesō_ means “please” (literally “I ask”).
distractors: _sedēte_ is to several people. To one person: _sedē_.
_sedet_ is “he sits”. A command to one person is _sedē_.

explain: _bibe_ is the command to one person from _bibō_. _vīnum_ is the object, accusative. _amīce_ is the vocative of _amīcus_.
distractors: _bibite_ is to several people. To one friend: _bibe_.
_bibit_ is “he drinks”. A command to one person is _bibe_.

en: I am preparing dinner for you.
explain: _tibi_ is the dative of _tū_: “to you, for you”. _cēnam_ is the object, accusative.
distractors: _tē_ is “you” as an object. “For you” is the dative: _tibi_.
_cēna_ is nominative. The thing you prepare is accusative: _cēnam_.

explain: _etiam_ means “yes” (literally “even so”). The question has _-s_ (you), so the answer has _-ō_ (I): _sitiō_.
distractors: _minimē_ means “no”, but the answer here is yes: _etiam_.

explain: Romans said “we give thanks to you”: _grātiās vōbīs agimus_. _vōbīs_ is the dative of “you all”, and _amīcī_ is the vocative plural.
distractors: _tibi_ is “to you” (one person). To several people: _vōbīs_.
When you speak to several people, use the vocative plural: _amīcī_.

explain: _vīs_ means “you want”, and _-ne_ makes it a question. _libenter_ is an adverb (“gladly”), so it never changes its ending.
distractors: _minimē_ means “not at all”. The answer is yes: _libenter_.

explain: To several people: _salvēte_ and _intrāte_. The ending _-te_ marks a command to a group.
distractors: _salvē_ is to one person. To several: _salvēte_.
_intrā_ is to one person. To several: _intrāte_.
Speaking to several people: vocative plural _amīcī_.

explain: Romans said _Bene vēnistī!_ (“You have come well”) to welcome someone, a perfect tense where English uses “welcome”. _vēnistī_ is the perfect of _veniō_, 2nd person singular.
distractors: _vēnistis_ is to several people. To one person: _vēnistī_.

en: I give you wine and bread.
explain: _tibi_ is the dative of _tū_: the person who receives. _vīnum et pānem_ are accusative: the things given.
distractors: _tē_ is “you” as an object. The person who receives is dative: _tibi_.
_pānis_ is nominative. The thing given is accusative: _pānem_.
